utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Which part do you want to have zoomed in?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The upper part. We can see two halves, but I am interested in the upper half because I am about to ask questions about it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Please take a look at the schematic and tell us what's missing here. Thank you. Is any unit missing in this schematic?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC
utterances.text: But which schematic? I apologise. And which part of it, the upper half, the lower half, all of it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The scheme is the same. One, the upper part, in B/C/S, the lower part in -- the lower, we can see here on the screen is in English. And Mr. Tolimir, as he did two hours ago, is asking you if there is something missing. I don't think that he is asking you about a unit attached to the commander himself. And you have it -- you have it in hard copy in front of you, Mr. Skrbic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may I start answering?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because a lot is missing in this schematic. I was in two minds as to whether this question referred to what we have already clarified. I am referring to the level where we see the names of General Milovanovic, Gvero, Djukic, and the others. Talking about this section, this is all correct. However, in the other horizontal part, where we read "1st Krajina Corps," "2nd Krajina Corps," and so on, at that level everything is all right, too. But the level which on the left begins with "67th Communications Regiment," it's in the lower left corner, this regiment is an independent unit of the Main Staff of the VRS. There is a lot of information missing at that level, and if I may I can tell you what.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I am not sure if Mr. Tolimir is referring to that question or not. You may continue and clarify your question, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I was asking what was missing from this schematic because his job description included the formation -- or, rather, the establishment structure. So I asked him for his opinion what was missing. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We all understood your question. Perhaps you can clarify it or make it a bit more specific so that the witness is not in a position to explain everything but the specific part you are interested in.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Skrbic, tell us which Main Staff units are missing here? Thank you. I mean units subordinated to the commander.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC
utterances.text: The 89th Artillery Rocket Brigade is missing. The 14th Logistics Base. The 27th Logistics Base. The 30th Logistics Base. The 35th Logistics Base. Furthermore, the airforce institute ORAO is missing. The technical maintenance institute Kosmos is missing. Then the technical maintenance institute Hadzici. The preventative medical institute is missing. The military medical centre. I am making a break for the interpreter to follow more easily. The military hospital of the Main Staff is also missing. The 410th Intelligence Centre. Furthermore, the counter-intelligence group. Then the military accounting centre. Then the military bookkeeping centre. Then the information and propaganda centre. The Manjaca training centre is also missing. The electronic data processing centre is missing. It wasn't fully active during the war, however, because the technical conditions had not been created. The central library of the VRS. The military orchestra.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, is this the kind of information you were asking for? Then you should please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. This is the information I wanted to elicit because this witness is most familiar with the establishment structure of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Just carry on, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Skrbic, I interrupted you, and now I am going to ask you about some things that I find most interesting in connection with these Main Staff units. What was the status of the 410th Intelligence Centre and the counter-intelligence group that you mentioned as missing from this schematic and which were subordinated to the commander? Thank you. I can amend my question: Who commanded and controlled these organisational units of the Main Staff, as far as you know? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC
utterances.text: The 410th Intelligence Centre and the counter-intelligence group were Main Staff institutes directly subordinate to the commander of the Main Staff of the VRS. That's why I listed them, Your Honours. I mentioned all of them to be comprehensive and accurate. I apologise if my answer was too lengthy.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Here is my question: Could anybody command the 410th Centre and the counter-intelligence group without the commander of the Main Staff knowing about it? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC
utterances.text: Without the knowledge and authorisation of the Main Staff commander nobody could command these two units.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did the Main Staff commander -- or could the Main Staff commander order the counter-intelligence group to take measures against General Tolimir or General Salapura or anybody from the intelligence and security administration without being duty-bound to inform these people, nor being held accountable for that decision?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC
utterances.text: Yes, he could issue such orders. According to the rules and regulations, he was not duty-bound to inform anybody about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. If he issued such orders to the counter-intelligence group to eavesdrop on Tolimir or anybody from his structure, did those who did it or could those who did it, were they allowed to inform the relevant persons about their activities?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC
utterances.text: I cannot explain it in this way. I can only explain the process. When the commander orders the 410th Intelligence Centre and the counter-intelligence group to do something, then they have to carry out the task and they don't inform anybody about it but the commander of the Main Staff, because they are directly subordinated to him. The specifics of their activities are not part of my expertise. I don't know if he ever issued such orders. But if the commander of the Main Staff issues them such orders, he can do so because that's part of his remit.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's please see the 65 ter document now. 2365 is the number, page 2 in the Serbian version and page 1 in the English version. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Skrbic, can you explain the nature of this document to us, the nature of this chart? What does it represent?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC
utterances.text: This document is a working plan. It contains all establishment elements, establishment duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. And is this document -- or was this document or plan drawn up in your sector, and if so, who was behind it? Which body or which individual? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC
utterances.text: This document was compiled in the sector at the -- that was under my responsibility. The document and information was compiled by officials, officers in my sector who were responsibility for personnel affairs. But you can see that this is a document created on a computer. A computer expert couldn't work on a computer without the information from officers who were under me. This document had the following purpose. It was for me and for the commander of the Main Staff so that it could be seen which positions had been filled and which hadn't been filled.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic. Let's briefly have a look at this chart. And could you first tell me what sort of information is contained in the chart? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's a little difficult for me to see. Would it be possible to enlarge the Serbian version? Although I know these things by heart to a large extent, but I wouldn't want to speak about it off the top of my head. That's fine. May I, Your Honour? I am starting from the top left-hand corner where you can see the term "establishment." Establishment -- under "establishment" you have "position," and then in the next box "rank." Under "rank" you have VES, you have that abbreviation which means "military specialty." And under the abbreviation VES you have the letters PG, that's "payroll group." That stands for "payroll group." And to the right, I think it means "position." In the next column you have "father's name," "family name." And then in the box further right you have the personal rank referred to and VES and the payroll group. In the next box to the right, it says: "Appointed by order of." And then in the next box to the right it says: "Registered in the following unit and institution." And in the final box to the right it says: "Remarks."

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Does this working chart include all those who are occupying establishment positions in the Main Staff or in some other unit?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC
utterances.text: Here you have only the actual situation that is depicted, and those individuals in this chart were actually in the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Does this working chart correctly depict the establishment of the Main Staff of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC
utterances.text: This working chart was compiled on the basis of a book on establishment. I have referred to certain elements which cannot be created, cannot be made up, and these elements were taken from a book on establishment.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see page 23 now in the e-court system. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in order to be of assistance for the e-court, this entire chart hasn't been translated. The translation is only partial, so I am afraid that the parts that we are now going to be using are not contained in the translated documents that we have in the e-court system.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: So the B/C/S version can be enlarged. Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you scroll up a bit so that I can see the part that you can't see on the screen right now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Do you see the title where it says: "Sector for intelligence and security"?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: In this part of the work chart that has to do with the intelligence and security sector, can you find information on the 410th Centre? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Could you tell us why no such information is to be found there?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC
utterances.text: Because the 410th Intelligence Centre wasn't part of the intelligence and security sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. And is there any information here on the sabotage unit and on the counter-intelligence group?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC
utterances.text: For the same reasons I have just mentioned, because they were not part of the sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see page 99, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: In the second column, above which it says: "The 66th Motorised Protection Regiment," can you see that part? "The 65th Regiment."

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, in the English it says "the 66th."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It's already corrected, 65th.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, I do apologise. Yes. I can see the 65th Motorised Protection Regiment. I do apologise, what was the question again?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I haven't put it yet. What was the status of this unit in the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC
utterances.text: The 65th Motorised Protection Regiment was a headquarter support unit in the Main Staff, directly subordinate to the commander of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. And what was the status of the Guards Motorised Brigade and who was it subordinated to? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC
utterances.text: The 1st Guards Motorised Brigade is not a headquarter support unit, but it is directly subordinated to the commander of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please see page 100. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Here we can see above the second column it says: "The 14th Logistics Base." How many such bases were there and what was their relationship with the logistics sector of the Main Staff? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC
utterances.text: There were four bases. I have already mentioned their names in my previous answer. These bases were also subordinated, directly subordinated to the commander of the Main Staff. They weren't part of the corps; although, they assisted the corps when it came to the logistics, having obtained authorisation to do so from the commander of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see now page 106. Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Above the second column, it says: "The 410th Intelligence Centre." Why can we find this in this part of the working chart? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC
utterances.text: Because it was a separate, independent institution of the Main Staff of the VRS, which was directly subordinated to the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did the commander exercise command and control over this body? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC
utterances.text: He did exercise command, that's for sure, but perhaps he transferred certain authorities to the sector for intelligence and security.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. And could the intelligence and security sector exercise command over the 410th Intelligence Centre?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC
utterances.text: No, it couldn't.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see page 108 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: If the interpreter heard correctly.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: At the bottom of the page of this chart, it says: "The Counter-Intelligence Group." My question is as follows -- well, now we have it there. Why [Realtime transcript read in error "where"] can we find this in this part of the working chart? If you could answer that question, please.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC
utterances.text: Because it was also an independent body within the Main Staff of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell me whether the military prosecution was independent of the VRS, or was it an integral part of the VRS and subordinated to someone?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC
utterances.text: Since this is an independent body I did not want to mention it, but within the Main Staff of the VRS there was also a military prosecutor's office with a lawyer Supic at its head. I don't know if he was judge. Nebojsa Supic. In judicial terms it was independent. It was dependent on the Main Staff only in terms of administrative issues. So it was an independent organisation, and the commander couldn't exercise command over the military prosecutor's office.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did the commander of the Main Staff and the command of the Main Staff have to comply with their requests so that this body could function properly? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Judge Nyambe has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Yes, I just need a clarification. At page 58, line 9 of today's transcript, the question was: "At the bottom of the page of this chart, it says: 'Counter-intelligence group.' My question is: Where can we find this in this part of the working chart?" And your answer is: "Because it was also an independent body of the VRS." The question doesn't follow. Is it my understanding that that is: "Why can we find this" rather than "where can we find this"? I don't know if I am clear.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I didn't say that it was part of the ministry. That's number one. And then I said that this counter-intelligence group was an independent institution, directly subordinated to the Main Staff commander. And I think the question was why is it entered in the chart as a separate entity, so you have separate entities such as corps and all the other institutions that I enumerated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Okay. So then we agreed that in line 10, the beginning of the sentence should be "why" rather than "where"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Why do we see that they are independent units, Your Honour? I'm sorry, I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: I don't think it's your problem. I think it's -- it should be a clarification from the interpretation. Was it "where" or was it "why"?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can we have line 9 back on the screen? It disappeared in the meantime. Thank you. May I assist, please. Look at the screen. Page 58, line 9 and 10. I don't know if you can read and understand the English transcript. In line 10, it says: "Where can we find this in this part of the working chart?" And Judge Nyambe is suggesting the better understanding would be of this question: "Why can we find this in this part of the working chart?" What is your position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Judge is right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I didn't want to interrupt, but Mr. Tolimir always asked why. That was the Defence question. Of course, I don't always think it is necessary for me to get up to have the record corrected because it is going to be revised anyway.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, could we just, for all our sakes, get an answer to - I am not sure it was your question - but the general's knowledge of English, just so we know? Because these sorts of things can be helpful, if we know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I didn't understand you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: You -- you basically, Your Honour, said: "I don't know if you can read and understand English transcript." But then he looked and he seems to have been able to answer the question. So can we just find out from the general how well he can speak and -- or read English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could you help us with that? Are you able to understand and speak English and read English?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very little, Your Honours. It's a very superficial knowledge that I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We must have our second break now, and we will resume quarter past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: There were, again, some discussions about the correct interpretation of some words in B/C/S, and I heard that the interpreters would be willing to assist us today if we put the three terms to them and to receive their interpretation in a very slow way. And these had to do with "control" and "command." And there were three terms. And, Mr. Tolimir, perhaps you can put these three terms we discussed about, just on the record, one-by-one. And after the first one, I would kindly ask the interpreters to give us their official translation.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I am grateful to Judge Nyambe for having noticed the discrepancy between the question and the answer, the interpretation thereof. Can we please have Exhibit P227 admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, can you just say the word and put it on the record what you -- the B/C/S word for "command."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Would you like me -- all right. We are going to tell the witness the following.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Please, we mentioned three terms here: "Komandovanje," "rukovodjenje," and "kontrola." Are all those synonyms or not? In command terms, do we have three different terms for three different operations? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: First of all, I would like to ask you if in lines 12 and 13 of page 62, the Serbian words are recorded correctly? If you please have a look on the screen and this transcript. Page 62, lines 12 and 13.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know what the word "redak" [phoen] means -- I mean I know what it means, but I don't know how it is marked in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please look at line 12. The last word, is that written correctly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And the following words, too?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Rukovodjenje" and "kontrola."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Are they written correctly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now I would kindly ask the interpreters to help us with their understanding, their correct translation. We start with "komandovanje."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "Command."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Then the next word, "rukovodjenje."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: In military terms it would be translated as "control," but in another context it can means things like "managing," "running, "administering," et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. And the third word is "kontrola."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "Control."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. This is, I think, all what we can do today for the sake of the transcript. Would the parties agree?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: I would like to ask the witness about the essence of these three terms in the B/C/S, and I would like the interpreters to bear that in mind. Mr. Skrbic, command, does it mean issuing oral and written orders to subordinate commands? Can you please explain the meaning of this word?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's leading. It's a simple question and an important one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Skrbic, what does the word "command" mean in military terms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The term "command" means the following: Oral and written issuing of tasks to units through documents and orders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. To avoid any misunderstanding, could you please explain the meaning of the word "rukovodjenje" in military terms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The term "control" contains processes that pertain to managing various professional areas. In that regard, plans, instructions, and directives, et cetera, can be issued.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. And please help us with your understanding of the word "kontrola" in military terms.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this word, "kontrola," I understand to mean the word that contains having an insight into the implementation and performance of the tasks that have been ordered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Tolimir, please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. If we have P227 in evidence, can we now look at another document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, before we call up another document, we have still on the screen 65 ter 2365. I was told that this document contains 108 pages, 15 of whom were translated into English. I don't know if you are going to tender it. I suppose so. We have seen on the screen one page which was translated into English, and then page 23, 99, 100, 106, and 108. These have no English translation yet and all the others have no translation yet. I would suggest, if you are tendering this document, that we only translate these pages you have used in the courtroom. They are part of your -- the evidence and your examination, and then we can mark these five pages for identification, pending translation. What is your position?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, as far as I am concerned I can accept that, but for the benefit of the Trial Chamber and everybody else who is going to refer to these pages and this document, I think that it would be advisable to have the whole document translated because that's an information that comes from the Main Staff and everybody who is interested in that will find it useful. The Defence believe this to be a crucial issue. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, 15 pages are already in English, and I think they will be helpful for a good understanding of the context of the whole document. I am not quite sure if you really need a translation of all the other pages because most of the entries in these tables are understandable and were not used in this trial. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. And many of the entries are handwritten and by the time it gets to CLSS it's very difficult for them to make it. And if -- we can get them better copies for the few pages. But it's much like a phone book. So the particular ones of interest, certainly, but the whole thing I don't think is necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It's really a burden for the translation unit. Would you agree to follow my proposal, Mr. Tolimir?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. President, it is difficult for me to agree. The question was: Why in this part of the flowchart do we find this or that unit. And we cannot tell whether it's a logistics structure or something else, and the one who will look at it will wonder where this protection regiment belongs or this unit or that because they are all in the separate parts. That's where they can be found and not in the first part. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Not to waste time with the witness, we will postpone a decision on that and review the pages we haven't seen yet in the meantime so that we are in a position to discuss it more properly at a later stage. Please continue with the next document, Mr. Tolimir. Yes, we could MFI the whole document and come back to that question later.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter document 2365 shall be assigned Exhibit D341, marked for identification. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please continue, Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Could we please see Exhibit P2520. Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Now we can see the document. This is document of the Main Staff of the VRS. The sector for organisation, mobilisation, and personal affairs. That was your sector. It was drafted on 12 July 1995. Did you draft this document and forward it? And when I say "you," I mean your organ. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to draw your attention to the line saying: "Assistant commander, Major-General Petar Skrbic." That's me. I signed it. And as to who drafted it, well, we would have to look at these initials that can poorly be seen in the original. Oh, I seem to have done something wrong now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can that part be zoomed in, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I am confused by these letters. It looks like a P and the following letter resembles a C, but I think I drafted it; whereas the other two initials must have been those of the person who typed it up. I don't remember who that was. But anyway, I -- I'm the author of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The document that we cannot see now because we zoomed in on the initials, could we have it back, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Does it say: "With the utmost urgency order the Sarajevo and Zvornik MO Secretariats to mobilise through the Pale, Sokolac, Rogatica, Visegrad, Han Pijesak, Vlasenica, Milici, Bratunac, and Zvornik MO departments all buses available in these municipalities. "At least 50 buses need to be mobilised and sent to Bratunac ... by 1400 hours on 12 July 1995 to the Bratunac sports stadium." And as you said, the signature block reads: "Assistant commander, Major-General Petar Skrbic." Thank you. Please explain to the Trial Chamber the nature of this document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, the sentence that in the translation begins with the words "At least 50 buses," there is a date, but I believe that it -- the date really should be the 13th and not the 12th, because it's impossible to -- it's impossible otherwise. No, it isn't legible even now. But it must be the 13th. I don't understand where this 12th in the English translation came from. All the rest was read out correctly. And the assistant who figures here is me. The question was about what it all means. This document is a request to the Ministry of Defence to mobilise 50 buses, and there is also information where the buses are needed and when, once they are mobilised.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Skrbic, why did you send this document to the Ministry of Defence? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC
utterances.text: Because under the law, the mobilisation of personnel and materiel is in the purview of the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please zoom in on the lower left-hand corner of the document. Thank you. Thank you. I apologise, I made a mistake. I meant the lower right-hand corner where the seal is, the stamp. Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Skrbic, is this an incoming or an outgoing document? Can you tell by looking at the dates -- at the date and time stated here? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC
utterances.text: This is an outgoing document. It emanated from the communications centre, the teleprinter operator who entered his personal information.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Please tell us from which location this cable was sent at? Was it from the Main Staff or was it from a logistics location? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC
utterances.text: This cable was sent from the communications centre, as I said, but from the teleprinter of the command post of logistics, because the centre where I --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The sector where I worked did not have such a device.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I don't think that there should be any major problems. In line 11 of page 69, it says "command post of the logistics." I think it should be "rear command post."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: What is the reason for your understanding?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, because that's what the witness said in Serbian, "pozadinsko komandno mesto," whereas this is a bit different. Logistics and what is called "pozadina" in Serbian need not coincide necessarily. As far as I was able to tell, the Serbian phrase that the witness used in his answer is often translated in documents shown here as "rear command post."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Skrbic, could you repeat, please, in Serbian how you referred to this post?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I called it "pozadinsko komandno mesto" which cannot be equaled to the logistical process because it's a command post in the rear, a rear command post.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the Serbian word, only the word itself, because it was not -- no, sorry, now we have a correction. If you could please look at page 70, line 5, in the middle. "I called it," you see there, and then a word. Can you confirm that this is written correctly or repeat it, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Pozadinsko."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: P-o-z-a-d-i-n-s-k-o.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But that was not all. That was only the first of three words.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The other two words were "komandno mesto," "command post."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We don't have it properly on the record. Could the interpreters please repeat the Serbian words, all the three of them.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I'll spell: "K-o-m-a-n-d-n-o." Second word, "m-e-s-t-o."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just to clarify this. Can we be told what in the stamp is the word that's crossed out with the two lines and what is the word that's underlined? Do they have anything to do with what he's saying or something else?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Skrbic, could you please read the second line of the stamp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I understand what you are pointing out to me, but I am unable to read it because the letters are not crisp and I wouldn't want to speculate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Skrbic, please tell us if the rear command post and the main command post of the Main Staff were at the same location? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC
utterances.text: The main command post was at Crna Rijeka and the rear command post was at Han Pijesak.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Was this telegram sent from the rear command post at Han Pijesak? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Please take a look at what is typed under the number halfway through the document. What does that mean? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC
utterances.text: You mean what's printed under "sector"? It says "Confidential number 39/31/13-3/154," and below that it's "12 July 1995."

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell us now what is printed to the right of the line of the confidential number?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC
utterances.text: It says "very urgent" in capital letters and double spaced.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. What does it mean to encryption operators when they get such a mark?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC
utterances.text: The teleprinter operator doesn't ask anybody but skips all other documents that are in process and immediately begins processing this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, on page 71, line 19, I think the number is not correct. It should say "09/31 ..." and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic, this kind of correction is a problem. I don't know what the witness said in Serbian. I heard exactly what the interpreters said. This is different from the English translation. I can't properly read the original. We all have to figure out at a later stage which is really the correct number. But we have now your position on the screen and on the record. Mr. Tolimir, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Skrbic, when you have a look at this telegram and its contents, can you say on the basis of this telegram when it was sent, on which date and at what time? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC
utterances.text: Could you please scroll up a bit? I can't see the whole document. I want to see the bottom part, the bottom page, and could you enlarge it, please? I can see it now. It was sent on the 12th of July, 1995, at 9.50, 0950 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. My question is as follows: Why did you draft this request? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC
utterances.text: Because an order was conveyed to me according to which it was necessary to urgently request that the Ministry of Defence mobilise buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you aware of the purpose for which buses were to be mobilised?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC
utterances.text: The buses were to be used to transport people. Naturally, it was important for me for these people to be mobilised and to arrive at the destinations they were supposed to arrive at on time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell us when you were informed that you should draft such a request to be forwarded to the Ministry of Defence? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC
utterances.text: I received this information on the 11th of July, 1995, in the evening hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please explain for the benefit of the Trial Chamber what tasks you subsequently carried out, if you did carry any tasks out?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. Having spoken to the person who informed me of this need, I phoned the Ministry of Defence and I informed the deputy minister of the request. The name of the person in question was Momo Kovacevic. He said, "Very well, general. But please write this request. Put this request in writing for me."

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Who has the right to request that buses be mobilised? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC
utterances.text: In this case only the commander of the Main Staff of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. Can anyone in the Main Staff, apart from the commander, request mobilisation of vehicles and can they submit this request to the individuals you mentioned? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC
utterances.text: No, not without the commander's authorisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see the following 65 ter document, 0014 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Stop, please. We are approaching the end of today's hearing, and I would like to put a question to the witness first. Sir, you said that you -- an order was conveyed to you to contact the Ministry of Justice and to send or to forward this request to the Ministry of Justice. Who informed you about this order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I cannot remember now. I cannot remember who informed me of this order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: By which means did you receive this information?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I received this information over the phone, the number of which is 250, extension 250. Only the commander can use this number or someone authorised by the commander. So I had no doubts about the fact that the information on that request had been authorised by the commander. I had no such doubts because this extension number was, in fact, used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: When you say "the commander," are you referring to General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Did this person who called you from this extension number inform you that it was a decision by or an order by the commander, Mladic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We are at the end of today's hearing. We will continue tomorrow. Please be reminded that you have -- are not permitted to have any contact to either party during the break before we continue tomorrow morning. We will resume at 9.00 in this courtroom, and we will adjourn now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: 7.00 p.m., to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 31st day of January, 2012, at 9.00 a.m.
